purpose: Auto-generated held-out decision benchmark (decision-bench-gen.py). Grounded in the brain's own corpus; spot-check before trusting fleet numbers.

cases.situation: You've spent years exercising obsessively and pursuing perfectionism, and you begin to notice the compulsive drive is damaging your relationships with the people closest to you, especially family. The behavior still produces admired outputs like achievement and discipline. Do you continue because the outputs look successful, or address the underlying pattern?
options: Continue the regimen since the visible achievements justify the personal cost
Enter residential therapeutic care to address the root belief system driving the compulsion
Cut back moderately on exercise hours but keep the same psychological approach
Seek a life coach rather than clinical therapy to preserve privacy
cases.actual_decision: Entered residential therapeutic care — five weeks across two stays — to address the root belief system driving the perfectionism
cases.actual_reasoning: The benefits of the compulsive drive were no longer close to compensating for the costs, which spread into relationships with the people closest to him, most importantly family.

cases.situation: You exercise 3-4 hours daily and follow the standard food pyramid guidelines precisely, yet you gain weight and develop insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome despite doing everything conventional medicine recommends. What do you do?
options: Increase exercise volume further and tighten dietary compliance to the pyramid
Conclude your genetics are simply unfavorable and accept the outcome
Abandon the conventional dietary framework and investigate the carbohydrate-insulin model of obesity
Consult a bariatric surgeon for intervention
cases.actual_decision: Abandoned the conventional dietary framework, investigated the carbohydrate-insulin model, and co-founded NuSI to fund rigorous nutrition science
cases.actual_reasoning: He was working too hard and busting his ass to be fit and healthy yet ending up in the worst shape of his life, which meant something in the standard model must be wrong.
cases.source: Hard Lessons: exercising obsessively while following food pyramid

cases.situation: As a young surgeon, you felt contempt for a diabetic patient needing a foot amputation, judging her as responsible for her own condition due to being overweight. Years later you come to doubt the causal model behind that judgment. How do you handle this realization publicly?
options: Keep the reflection private and simply change your future clinical behavior
Publicly apologize to the patient in a TED Talk and restructure your framework around obesity as cause vs symptom
Write an academic paper correcting the record without personal disclosure
Avoid revisiting the incident to prevent reputational damage
cases.actual_decision: Publicly apologized to the patient in a TED Talk and restructured his framework around whether obesity is a cause or symptom of metabolic disease
cases.actual_reasoning: He gave her his best clinical care but treated her with contempt as a human being, and came to believe insulin resistance rather than behavioral failure may be the real cause, warranting public accountability.

cases.situation: You've written the first full version of your longevity book as a comprehensive, technically exhaustive document without narrative structure. The publisher tells you it's unpublishable — too technical, no story. What do you do?
options: Push back and insist the technical depth is the book's core value
Rewrite the book twice more, shifting toward narrative and reader-focused structure
Self-publish the original technical version independently
Hire a ghostwriter to add narrative elements to the existing draft
cases.actual_decision: Rewrote the book twice more (three total versions over six years), making it shorter and more narrative-driven
cases.actual_reasoning: Writing forces the question of whether each element is necessary and helps the reader understand something; shorter and more narrative proved structurally better than technically exhaustive.
cases.source: Hard Lessons: Outlive first draft rejected

cases.situation: You planned a comprehensive pharmacology appendix in your book covering about 20 drugs, hormones, and supplements — including rapamycin, metformin, and NMN — at 8-10 pages each. This would add roughly 200 pages to a 450-page book, and the publisher objects. What do you do?
options: Insist on keeping the full 200-page appendix as essential reference material
Cut the appendix significantly to meet publisher length constraints
Self-publish the appendix separately as a companion document
Convert the appendix into a subscription-only online resource instead
cases.actual_decision: Materially reduced the appendix content to satisfy publisher constraints on total book length
cases.actual_reasoning: The publisher rejected a 200-page appendix on a 450-page book, forcing him to cut back the planned comprehensive drug/supplement reference.

cases.situation: You've just delivered genetic testing results to a client showing he carries the APOE4 allele, the strongest known genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease — dramatically raising his lifetime risk. How do you frame this alarming result to him?
options: Present it neutrally as clinical data without additional commentary
Frame it as a motivational catalyst, telling him aggressive preventive action can reduce his risk to that of anyone else
Recommend he not dwell on it since current interventions have limited proven efficacy
Refer him to a genetic counselor rather than discuss it directly yourself
cases.actual_decision: Framed it as a motivational gift, telling Hemsworth that with every possible preventive step, his risk could be reduced to that of anyone else
cases.actual_reasoning: Attia believes that emphasizing actionability converts a potentially paralyzing genetic diagnosis into a catalyst for behavior change rather than despair.

cases.situation: You want to complete an extremely ambitious open-water swim of 20-25 miles, a distance that feels psychologically impossible to approach directly. How do you build toward it?
options: Attempt to plan the full 20-25 mile distance from the outset with a rigid long-term training schedule
Swim a shorter proof-of-concept distance first (two miles) to establish that scaling up is an engineering problem, not an impossible feat
Hire an elite open-water coach immediately to design the entire program before swimming at all
Abandon the extreme goal in favor of a more modest, clearly achievable swim distance
cases.actual_decision: Swam two miles in open water first as a proof-of-concept milestone before scaling toward the 20-25 mile goal
cases.actual_reasoning: Completing the two-mile swim unlocked the belief that the larger distance was a scalable engineering problem rather than an impossible feat.

cases.situation: Having developed insulin resistance despite heavy exercise and pyramid-compliant eating, you want to test whether macronutrient composition matters more than calories or exercise volume. What do you do?
options: Increase exercise volume even further while keeping the same diet to force weight loss
Dramatically change diet — restricting refined grains and sugar — while simultaneously reducing exercise volume
Hire a personal trainer to optimize the existing high-volume exercise regimen
Undergo bariatric surgery to bypass the metabolic issue directly
cases.actual_decision: Dramatically restricted refined grains and sugar while reducing exercise volume, losing 20 kg
cases.actual_reasoning: This personal experiment provided strong anecdotal evidence that macronutrient composition rather than caloric expenditure was driving his metabolic dysfunction.
cases.source: Documented Choices: self-experiment diet and exercise

cases.situation: You notice large, unexplained swings in your own lipid panel that don't correspond to any dietary or medication changes you've made. You eventually trace it to an ignored dental abscess. What conclusion do you draw about standard lipid measurement practice?
options: Conclude lipid panels are simply noisy and not worth tracking closely
Conclude that inflammation must be controlled for when interpreting lipid measurements, since infection alone caused large swings
Assume lab error and request repeat testing without further investigation
Attribute the swings to normal biological variability unrelated to any specific cause
cases.actual_decision: Concluded that inflammation dramatically alters lipoprotein markers and that standard lipid measurements must account for inflammatory state
cases.actual_reasoning: The dental abscess demonstrated that lipid panels taken without controlling for inflammation can be misleading, independent of diet or drugs.
cases.source: Documented Choices: dental abscess and lipid swings

cases.situation: You are trained as a surgical oncologist within elite academic institutions, having seen firsthand how conventional medicine only intervenes at end-stage, symptomatic disease. You believe intervention needs to happen decades earlier, but this approach lacks institutional validation and pays off only on a 20-30 year time horizon academic incentives don't support. What career path do you pursue?
options: Remain in academic surgical oncology and push for reform from within
Leave academic surgery to build an independent practice around prevention rather than treatment
Transition into pharmaceutical industry research on late-stage disease treatments
Pursue a public health policy role focused on population-level guideline reform
cases.actual_decision: Left academic surgery to build a private practice/clinic (Early Medical) organized around prevention-first, proactive longevity medicine
cases.actual_reasoning: Operating at the extreme end of Medicine 2.0 crystallized his conviction that intervention at the symptomatic stage is too late, requiring him to build outside institutional validation despite the long time horizon.

cases.situation: You want to teach complex, evolving medical reasoning about longevity to a broad public audience, not just deliver polished conclusions. What medium and format do you choose?
options: Write short, digestible blog posts summarizing conclusions
Launch a long-form podcast featuring in-depth conversations with researchers that models the full inferential process in real time
Produce short social media video clips with simplified takeaways
Publish peer-reviewed papers translated into accessible summaries
cases.actual_decision: Launched The Drive podcast in 2018, using long-form audio conversations with researchers and clinicians
cases.actual_reasoning: Long-form audio allowed him to model the full inferential process, not just conclusions, creating a public record of his evolving thinking and holding him accountable to intellectual consistency.
cases.source: Biography: 2018 Launch of The Drive podcast

cases.situation: During performance activities like archery, you notice yourself spiraling into destructive self-criticism and rage whenever you make a mistake. You want a concrete behavioral intervention to interrupt this pattern in the moment. What do you do?
options: Simply try to suppress the anger through willpower in the moment
Pull out your phone and audibly record a voice memo narrating the situation as if it happened to a friend
Stop the activity immediately whenever the rage begins to avoid reinforcing the pattern
Schedule a debrief with a therapist after each session rather than intervening in real time
cases.actual_decision: Recorded a voice memo narrating the situation aloud as if it happened to a friend, at the edge of destructive self-criticism
cases.actual_reasoning: Narrating the situation as if it happened to a friend creates distance from the default self-critical reaction and interrupts the rage pattern in real time.

cases.situation: You want to improve your eating habits and reduce time spent on unproductive behaviors, but you're unsure whether to focus energy on eliminating the bad behaviors directly or on something else. What approach do you take?
options: Focus primarily on identifying and eliminating bad habits one by one
Focus on building new good habits, trusting they will naturally displace the old ones
Use strict punishment/reward systems to suppress bad behaviors
Address bad habits and good habits simultaneously with equal emphasis
cases.actual_decision: Focused on building good behaviors, which necessarily displace old bad ones
cases.actual_reasoning: Good habits crowd out bad ones in a zero-sum dynamic, like a plant spreading its leaves to absorb more light — displacement works better than direct suppression.
leak_markers: building or establishing new good behaviors
cases.source: Documented Choices: habit building displaces bad habits

cases.situation: You want to read more but find yourself defaulting to distracting apps on your phone instead. What environmental change do you make to increase the likelihood of reading?
options: Delete all distracting apps entirely from the phone
Move the audiobook app to the home screen and push distracting apps to a secondary screen
Set a strict daily time limit on all non-reading apps using screen time controls
Switch to a physical book only and leave the phone in another room
cases.actual_decision: Moved Audible to the home screen and relocated other apps to the second screen
cases.actual_reasoning: Digital environments follow the same design principles as physical ones — reducing friction to the desired behavior and increasing friction to the competing behavior meaningfully increases engagement with the good behavior.
cases.source: Documented Choices: digital environment habit engineering

cases.situation: You're preparing for your freshman year of college over the summer. You want to maximize your ability to engage deeply with the material once classes begin. What do you do the summer before?
options: Relax over the summer and prepare mentally without academic work
Buy all the freshman-year math and physics textbooks and work through them independently before classes start
Take a light summer course at a local college to get a head start on credits
Focus summer preparation on extracurricular and social readiness instead of academics
cases.actual_decision: Bought all the freshman textbooks for math and physics and worked through them independently over the summer
cases.actual_reasoning: This meant he effectively completed every course twice, allowing him to engage with material at a far deeper level than peers encountering it for the first time.

cases.situation: During cold water immersion, you experience waves of adrenaline that make the experience psychologically difficult to endure. How do you frame the experience mentally to make it more sustainable?
options: Focus on counting down a fixed time duration until the immersion ends
Frame it as passing through successive waves of adrenaline like walls, rather than enduring a fixed duration
Distract yourself entirely by thinking about unrelated topics during immersion
Use breathing exercises exclusively without any cognitive reframing
cases.actual_decision: Framed the experience as going through successive waves/walls of adrenaline rather than enduring a time duration
cases.actual_reasoning: Thinking of it as walls of adrenaline to pass through, rather than a fixed time to endure, makes the experience psychologically more manageable and sustainable.
cases.source: Documented Choices: cold exposure adrenaline framing

cases.situation: You've committed to a meditation practice but find yourself struggling to follow it consistently, sometimes skipping sessions entirely out of frustration with imperfect execution. What approach do you take?
options: Push through with the original rigorous program despite the struggle, treating any deviation as failure
Lower the bar for success progressively until adherence becomes possible, then gradually raise it again
Abandon meditation altogether in favor of another emotional health practice
Hire a meditation teacher to enforce stricter accountability on the original program
cases.actual_decision: Lowered the bar for success progressively, treating consistency over perfection as the goal
cases.actual_reasoning: A consistent but imperfect practice is categorically superior to a perfect program that gets abandoned; the bar should be lowered until adherence is possible, then gradually raised.
cases.source: Documented Choices: meditation consistency over perfection

cases.situation: In 2020, you face a second significant psychological crisis, involving renewed confrontation with depression and the fragility of the psychological architecture you built after your first crisis in 2017. How do you frame and respond to this recurrence?
options: View it as evidence that the earlier therapeutic work had failed and abandon that approach entirely
Return to residential intensive therapy again, treating the setback as part of an ongoing process rather than failure
Handle it privately through self-directed coping strategies without returning to formal treatment
Seek a different treatment modality entirely, having lost confidence in the prior approach
cases.actual_decision: Returned to residential intensive therapy for a second stay (three weeks in 2020, following two weeks in 2017)
cases.actual_reasoning: Difficult periods are ingredients of growth, not obstacles to it — the ability to hold perspective during setbacks as part of the process rather than evidence of failure is what allowed him to return to intensive treatment rather than abandon it.
cases.source: Documented Choices: second 2020 psychological crisis; residential intensive therapy
